title: PostgreSQL Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the PostgreSQL course.

entries.name: Ask the database a question
entries.summary: A SELECT query can calculate a value without reading a table.

entries.name: Make a practice table
entries.summary: A table names the facts each row can hold.

entries.name: Return an inserted value
entries.summary: RETURNING asks PostgreSQL to show values from a row it has just changed.

entries.name: Search text without letter case
entries.summary: ILIKE is PostgreSQL's case-insensitive pattern match.

example.code:
WITH books(title) AS (VALUES ('Moon Trip'),('Garden Days'))
SELECT title FROM books WHERE title ILIKE 'moon%';

entries.name: Sort before taking a few rows
entries.summary: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then restricts how many of those rows are returned.

example.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES ('Moon Trip',60),('Garden Days',40),('Tiny Seed',20))
SELECT title,pages FROM books ORDER BY pages,title LIMIT 2;

entries.name: Count rows in each group
entries.summary: GROUP BY puts matching values together. An aggregate such as count gives one answer for each group.

example.code:
WITH books(kind) AS (VALUES ('story'),('science'),('story'))
SELECT kind,count(*) AS book_count FROM books GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind;

entries.name: Join related facts
entries.summary: A join matches rows using a shared value.

entries.name: Keep a change in a transaction
entries.summary: A transaction groups changes into one job.

entries.name: Read a JSONB field
entries.summary: JSONB stores JSON data in a form PostgreSQL can query.

entries.name: Use an array for a small value list
entries.summary: PostgreSQL can store an array of values.

entries.name: Number rows without grouping them
entries.summary: A window function calculates across related rows while keeping each row visible.

example.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES ('Moon Trip',60),('Tiny Seed',20))
SELECT title,row_number() OVER (ORDER BY pages,title) AS reading_order FROM books ORDER BY reading_order;

entries.name: Read a query plan first
entries.summary: EXPLAIN shows how PostgreSQL plans to run a query.

example.code: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM pg_books WHERE id=1;
